SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset severe left-sided headache since 05:30 today; woke patient from sleep; persistent at time of call.
  • Prior headaches: intermittent, less severe, frontal “cluster”; never this intense or unilateral.
  • Associated symptoms today:
    – Mild photophobia.
    – Brief morning dizziness (resolved).
    – No neck stiffness, fever, or nausea.
    – Pain initially worse on lying down, then eases; overall better when supine.
  • Analgesia tried: Paracetamol (dose/frequency not documented) with no relief.
- Stressors: High work stress for ~2 months; late nights.
- Past medical history: Generalized anxiety disorder (≈2 yrs).
- Medications:
  • Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • Paracetamol (prn, today only).
- Social history:
  • Lives with partner; non-smoker; runs ≥3×/week; owns a cat.
  • Diet “okay,” not particularly healthy; recent poor sleep due to work.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA).
- Family history: Mother with anxiety; no migraine history.

Objective:
- No in-person examination; no vitals recorded (telephone consultation).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache
   - Assessment: Likely tension-type headache vs migraine.
   - Differential diagnosis: Migraine (left-sided pain, photophobia).
   - Investigations planned:
     • None immediately; consider blood tests if no improvement at follow-up.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Start ibuprofen (higher migraine-appropriate dosing; specific dose not documented).
     • Continue/paracetamol as needed.
     • Hydration goal: 1.5–2 L water daily (excluding caffeinated drinks).
     • Sleep hygiene: target 7–8 h/night.
     • Provide written information on headache “red flag” symptoms; low threshold to re-contact clinic if worsening.
   - Follow-up: Telephone review in 1 week.

2. Work-related stress / Anxiety
   - Assessment: Ongoing work stress contributing to headache; chronic anxiety on sertraline.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Advise taking up to 1 week off work (self-certification).
     • Provide self-referral link to local counseling service.
   - Relevant referrals: Counseling/psychological therapies service (self-referral details to be sent).

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: No vital signs or neurological exam documented; sertraline and analgesic dosages not provided; no medication reconciliation beyond stated drugs.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; no significant inaudible sections.
